A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VTEdit-Bench and VTEdit-QA work, and all supplied pages, equations, tables, and figures were readable. V1 includes Appendices A–B; v2 ends after the references and omits that material despite retaining supplementary cross-references. This is an observable document difference, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of eight universal editors and seven specialized VTON models, human-preference annotations, evaluator correlations, and supplementary qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark experiments and human-correlation results and adds an analysis of benchmark attribute distributions.

M1.justification: Both versions use GPT-4o to score model consistency, cloth consistency, and image quality on a 0–5 scale, then take their minimum. The Bradley–Terry annotation pipeline also remains unchanged. Omitted prompt templates do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both retain the same five tasks, source datasets, and 24,220 test pairs. V2's new attribute-distribution figure characterizes existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2–4 is unchanged. However, v2 omits the Qwen automatic-evaluator comparison against GPT-4o reported in v1 Appendix A.3 and Table 5. This is distinct from Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, which remains in the editing benchmark.

E3.justification: The retained experiments specify unchanged task counts and splits, zero-shot evaluation, official specialized-model checkpoints, FID/KID metrics, and human-ranking/SRCC procedures. The missing supplementary prompts and preprocessing recipes reduce documentation without establishing revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: V2 omits v1's evaluator-validation analyses comparing individual dimensions, mean versus minimum aggregation, and GPT-4o versus Qwen, together with extended failure analyses and comparative examples in Appendix B. It adds a dataset-attribute analysis in Section 3.1/Figure 3, but substantial evidence testing evaluator choices and model failure behavior is no longer included.

E5.justification: Both retain three annotators, over 15,000 annotations, Bradley–Terry estimation, and SRCC reporting. Neither reports model-run uncertainty, seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The omitted correlation entries are result losses rather than changes in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 2–4 and the headline SRCC values of 0.75 and 0.72 are unchanged. However, v2 removes substantial supplementary evidence, including Qwen's correlations of 0.68/0.57/0.64, individual-dimension and mean-aggregation correlations, and additional scored visual comparisons. Figure 3 newly reports benchmark attribute proportions.

T1.justification: The Bradley–Terry probability formula, maximum-likelihood ranking description, and SRCC definition remain unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and evaluator claims: five increasingly complex tasks, competitive universal editors with stronger generalization in harder settings, and persistent identity and multi-item composition limitations.

C2.justification: The main discussion and limitations remain unchanged. V2 loses Appendix A.3's specific interpretations that image-quality scores alone poorly track human preferences and that GPT-4o is a better evaluator than Qwen. It adds a limited discussion of dominant and challenging dataset attributes.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link but omits the auxiliary-input generation recipes, per-model condition requirements, complete evaluator rubrics and output format, and exact unified editing prompt from v1 Appendices A.1–A.2 and B.1–B.2. These are substantial reproducibility-documentation losses; the PDFs do not establish what the linked project supplies.

R1.justification: V2 removes the OpenPose, Detectron2, and HR-VITON preprocessing-tutorial references associated with the omitted supplement. The remaining cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence are retained. V2 modestly rewrites and expands Section 3.1, corrects terminology and cross-references, expands author affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. Appendices A–B are no longer included, without a broader rewrite of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adds the attribute-distribution Figure 3 and removes the supplementary displays in v1 Figures 7–11 and Tables 5–6. All six original main-text graphics are retained, with renumbering, an enlarged correlation chart, and a revised evaluator-example caption. Tables 3–4 are relocated together onto one page.

improvement.justification: V2 improves dataset characterization and adds a project link, but the supplied PDF loses the explicit prompts, preprocessing instructions, evaluator-choice validation, and extended comparative evidence provided by v1's appendices. These omissions substantially weaken reproducibility and readers' ability to assess the central evaluator, while references still direct readers to absent supplementary material. Those losses outweigh the limited explanatory and presentation gains.
